walkthrough:
Integrate $\frac{dy}{dx} = 3(4x+5)^{1/2}$ with respect to $x$ using the reverse chain rule:
$$y = \int 3(4x+5)^{1/2}\,dx = 3 \cdot \frac{(4x+5)^{3/2}}{\frac{3}{2} \cdot 4} + c = \frac{3}{6}(4x+5)^{3/2} + c = \frac{1}{2}(4x+5)^{3/2} + c$$

Substitute the point $(1,9)$ into the curve equation to determine the constant $c$:
$$9 = \frac{1}{2}(4(1)+5)^{3/2} + c \implies 9 = \frac{1}{2}(9)^{3/2} + c \implies 9 = \frac{1}{2}(27) + c$$
$$c = 9 - \frac{27}{2} = -\frac{9}{2}$$

Write the complete equation of the curve:
$$y = \frac{1}{2}(4x+5)^{3/2} - \frac{9}{2}$$

Substitute $x = 5$ into the curve equation to calculate the value of $a$:
$$a = \frac{1}{2}(4(5)+5)^{3/2} - \frac{9}{2} = \frac{1}{2}(25)^{3/2} - \frac{9}{2} = \frac{1}{2}(125) - \frac{9}{2} = \frac{116}{2} = 58$$
